T.topic_fa: میبلین بعد از ۳۵ سال شعار معروفش را عوض کرد: «شاید ذاتی است، شاید میبلین است» با دو نقطه و یک ضمیر تازه شد یک بیانیه، و اینترنت شلوغ شد
T.topic_en: Maybelline rewrote its 35-year-old line. Two full stops and one pronoun turned the most hummable question in beauty into a statement, and the internet pushed back
T.central_tension_fa: فکر می‌کنیم شعار با پیام واضح‌تر قوی‌تر می‌شود؛ ولی قدرت این شعار در شکش بود. «شاید» یک سؤال بود با چشمک. میبلین سؤال را با دو نقطه بست، و مردم حس کردند چیزی را که بلد بودند بخوانند از دستشان گرفته‌اند.
T.central_tension_en: We think a clearer message makes a stronger slogan. This one was strong because it was a question with a wink. Maybelline closed the question with two full stops, and people felt a line they could sing had been taken from them.
T.working_hook_fa: میبلین فقط دو نقطه به شعارش اضافه کرد. همین کافی بود.
T.working_hook_en: Maybelline added two full stops to its slogan. That was enough.

key_sources.claim: Old: 'Maybe she's born with it. Maybe it's Maybelline.' (since 1991). New: 'Maybe. We're born with it. Maybe. It's Maybelline.' Punctuation makes it 'more like a declaration'; 'we're' to include all women; permanent change.
PeakMetrics: mentions peaked at 68x typical volume; 48% negative, 28% positive, 24% neutral; ~a quarter object to wording/punctuation; 38% jokes or sarcasm.
'Four sentences where there used to be two'; brand president: the original was 'giving ambiguity – it was more of a question.'
Allen Adamson: the words are 'so hardwired to Maybelline that they can't walk away from it.'

T.framing_note: Type 1 (famous-brand controversy). Spine: (1) everyone can sing it: 'Maybe she's born with it. Maybe it's Maybelline.' (2) The trick was the doubt: born with it, or makeup? A question with a wink; even the brand president says the old line was 'more of a question'. (3) Nov 2026: 'Maybe. We're born with it. Maybe. It's Maybelline.' One pronoun, two full stops; two sentences became four. (4) Reaction: one social-listening firm counted mentions at 68x normal, about half negative; many joked it reads like a hostage statement (attribute as a critic's line, not ours). (5) Why it hurt: you can't punctuate a jingle; people don't read a slogan, they sing it; the full stop killed the rhythm and the question. (6) Fair side, once: the brand's intent ('we' = every woman; 'maybe' = possibility) is reasonable, and no one knows yet if it hurts sales. (7) Lesson: before you fix your famous line, find out what people actually remember about it; often the flaw is the asset. Rules: show the words as typography (the renderer sets them; never an AI-drawn logo); no Miley Cyrus or any face; do not take a political side on the 'inclusivity' framing (keep it out of the on-screen copy; caption may mention critics framed it politically, neutrally); say 'one social-listening firm' not 'everyone hated it'; do not name who wrote the 1991 line. Distinguish from 2026-11-25 (Black Friday name): that was about a name the public gave; this is about a brand editing its own sung line. Never name the UAE, Dubai or any emirate.

A slogan is sung, not read: the rhythm is the asset
Two full stops stamped a question into a statement
They erased the question mark that was never written
